seo_title: Gojek Case Study: B2B Content in Singapore | SOMIN
description: SOMIN read 5,967 pieces of 2023-24 media from 6 Singapore mobility brands for Gojek: Gojek made 76.79% of the B2B content, but Grab spoke more to employees.
eyebrow: Brand case study · B2B transport · Singapore
h1: Gojek makes 76.79% of B2B mobility content, but Grab sounds more human
lede: For Gojek, SOMIN read 5,967 pieces of paid and organic media that 6 Singapore mobility brands published in 2023 and 2024, then isolated the business-to-business content. Gojek produced 76.79% of it, yet Grab ran a lot more creative variations and spoke more about employees. The briefing mapped 5 B2B personas, 5 topics and the challenges each brand tried to solve.
meta_line: A SOMIN brand briefing · 2023 to 2024 · Singapore · B2B audiences

challenge.title: How 6 Singapore mobility brands talk to business customers
challenge.body: Gojek's Singapore content library held 8,363 pieces of paid and organic media across 6 mobility brands, dating from 2016 to 2024. The question was how the industry had been addressing businesses recently: what B2B content looked like in 2023 and 2024, who it targeted and what it tried to solve.

approach.title: 5,967 pieces of media, filtered to B2B and clustered four ways
points: Filtered the library to 2023 and 2024: 5,967 pieces of media, 3,703 paid and 2,264 organic, with 1,546 unique captions.
Split business-to-business content from consumer content: B2B was 18.85% of all content and 30.25% of ads, and almost all of it ran as ads.
Clustered the B2B content into personas, topics, relevance themes and challenges with SOMIN's semantic models.
Compared total media with unique media for each brand, to separate sheer volume from creative variety.
Combined one persona and one challenge into a data-driven story with society, economic and psychology angles.

findings_title: Volume, variety and employee themes in Gojek and Grab's B2B ads

findings.title: Two brands own B2B
findings.body: Gojek ran 867 pieces of B2B content (76.79%) and Grab 258 (22.85%). ComfortDelGro had 4, and Maxi Cab, Ryde and TADA had none.

findings.title: Volume is not variety
findings.body: Gojek's total may be inflated by DCO and multi-variant targeting. On unique media, Grab has a lot more variations, which lets it test what works.

findings.title: Grab talks about people
findings.body: Grab talks more about employee benefits, recognition and satisfaction, and is the only brand discussing security in B2B. It also dominates the voucher space.

delivered.title: 5 B2B personas, 5 topics and 4 challenge clusters for Gojek
points: 5 B2B personas, led by Efficiency Innovators (770 media), Efficiency Enthusiasts (206) and Financial Empowerment Champions (144)
5 topic clusters, from efficient business transport and expense management (940 media) to digital gift vouchers for businesses
6 relevance themes and 4 challenge clusters, each split by brand for total and unique media
Analyst notes on the charts, including outliers such as Thai-language content and a fire announcement post
A story generator output: one persona and one challenge turned into a character, angles and a short story

quote.text: It is possible to have too much of a good thing if it blinds you to the needs of those who make it all possible.

outcome.title: Gojek should make B2B efficiency sound human
outcome.body: The briefing recommends exploring employee satisfaction angles, a big issue for many companies and a space Grab already tries to capitalise on. Running more unique variations would also let Gojek test which B2B angles work, rather than relying on volume.

faq.q: What data did SOMIN use for the Gojek case?
faq.a: A Singapore content library of 8,363 pieces of paid and organic media from 6 mobility brands, dating from 2016 to 2024. The B2B analysis used the 5,967 pieces from 2023 and 2024, with paid media tracked from 19 September 2023.
ComfortDelGro, Gojek, Grab, Maxi Cab, Ryde and TADA. Only Gojek, Grab and ComfortDelGro ran B2B content in 2023 and 2024.

faq.q: How were the B2B personas found?
faq.a: SOMIN clustered the content with an X-means algorithm on ADA embeddings, using its audience, topic and insight semantic models. The result was 5 personas, 5 topics, 6 relevance themes and 4 challenges.
